paper.paper_scope: Investigates the co-precipitation behavior and mechanism of Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide precipitates in Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C-(0,3)Cu austenitic low-density steel after solution treatment (1000°C/1h) and aging (550°C/3h), focusing on how Cu addition and κ-carbide affect Cu-rich phase precipitation and the orientation relationship with the austenitic matrix.
paper.title: Co-precipitation mechanism of Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide precipitates in Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C-3Cu austenitic low-density steel

processes.processes_notes: This process is applied to both the 0Cu and 3Cu steels and is the parent state for the subsequent aging treatment.

unmapped_findings: Adding Cu to Fe-28Mn-10Al-1C austenitic low-density steel increases the austenitic matrix lattice parameter, which is beneficial for κ-carbide precipitation; Cu-rich phase and κ-carbide are the main precipitates of the Fe-Mn-Al-C-Cu low-density steel.

Under solution treatment the austenitic matrix lattice parameter is a = 0.3687 nm for 0Cu steel and a = 0.3689 nm for 3Cu steel, both higher than the critical lattice parameter (~0.3670 nm) required for intragranular κ-carbide precipitation.
According to formula 0.208(wt.%C) + 0.098(wt.%Al) = 1 - 0.0054(wt.%Mn), the critical Al content for κ-carbide precipitation in 0Cu steel is 6.52 wt%, which the steel's Al content exceeds.

The Cu-rich phase was determined to have an FCC structure (crystal plane spacing (002) = 0.182 nm, lattice parameter a = 0.3652 nm), while the κ-carbide lattice parameter is a = 0.3775 nm; SAED indicated the Cu-rich phase has BCC structure in Fig. 1 (inset).
Lattice misfits: κ-carbide/Cu-rich phase = 3.4%, κ-carbide/austenite = 2.3%, Cu-rich phase/austenite = 1.0%, all below 5% indicating coherent relationships.

The κ-carbide and Cu-rich phase have a cube-on-cube orientation relationship with the austenitic matrix: [110]γ//[110]κ//[110]Cu and (111)γ//(111)κ//(111)Cu; κ-carbide precipitates earlier than Cu-rich phase during aging and promotes its precipitation.
